name: they/them
history: Singular “they” has been used in English to describe an unspecified person {#link to=|https://www.academicwritingsuccess.com/the-astonishing-history-of-singular-they/|}since the late 1300s{/link} (it's even older than singular “you”!). Nowadays, it's the most popular choice among people who prefer gender neutral forms. It starts being {#link to=|https://www.merriam-webster.com/words-at-play/singular-nonbinary-they|}accepted by dictionaries{/link} too.{#break/}It is also common to use {#link to=|/they/them/themself|}“themself”{/link} as a reflexive form.
sourcesInfo: This list of sources includes both the version with {#link to=|/they|}“themselves”{/link} and {#link to=|/they/them/themselves|}“themself”{/link}, as well as those that don't happen to use reflexive.
examples: I think they are very nice.
They told me that the house is theirs.
They said they would rather do it themselves.
They take good care of their cat.
They did it all by themselves.
Did you buy them their gift?
I asked them if I can borrow their pencil.
Would you like to go to the movies with them?
Can you call them when their cat awakes?
My favorite color is purple, theirs is yellow.
